candidate.educational_objective: Explain that patient-safety event reports are used for organizational learning and system-level safety improvement rather than automatic blame or replacement of clinical care.

options.A: Automatically assign disciplinary action to the staff member involved
options.B: Replace the need for immediate clinical management of the patient
options.C: Support organizational learning, identify system vulnerabilities, and guide safety improvement
options.D: Serve as the patient's routine clinical progress documentation

candidate.rationale: AHRQ describes patient-safety event reporting as a core method for detecting safety events and quality problems and emphasizes using reports within a larger patient-safety system to learn from events and improve system performance. A blame-focused approach can inhibit reporting and safety improvement. Event reporting does not replace immediate patient care or routine clinical documentation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Event reporting systems help detect safety events and quality problems and support learning and system improvement; blame-focused approaches inhibit reporting and improvement.
